lines.name: Advance Variation

notes.1: …e6 prepares …d5, with a pawn ready to recapture on d5.
notes.5: …c5 strikes at d4, the base of White's pawn chain.
notes.9: …Qb6 piles up on d4 and eyes the b2 pawn.
notes.11: …c4 clamps the queenside, taking b3 and d3 away from White.

lines.summary: Attack the base of the chain: …c5, …Nc6 and …Qb6 all hit d4.

lines.name: Exchange Variation

notes.5: …exd5 gives a symmetrical structure, and Black's light-squared bishop is free.
notes.9: …Bd6 mirrors White's development; the position is level.

lines.summary: Symmetrical and calm: develop naturally and castle.

lines.name: Winawer Variation

notes.5: …Bb4 pins the c3 knight, adding pressure on e4.
notes.7: …c5 hits the d4 pawn, the classic French counter.
notes.9: …Bxc3+ gives up the bishop to double White's c-pawns.
notes.11: …Ne7 develops and keeps the f-pawn free; the knight can go to f5 or c6.

lines.summary: Pin with …Bb4, hit d4 with …c5, then trade on c3 to damage White's pawns.

lines.name: Tarrasch: Open (3…c5)

notes.5: …c5 hits the centre at once; Black accepts an isolated d-pawn for active pieces.
notes.9: …Nc6 develops and adds pressure on d4.

lines.summary: Meet 3.Nd2 with …c5: active pieces in return for an isolated d-pawn.

lines.name: Classical: 4.Bg5

notes.7: …Be7 breaks the pin on the f6 knight.
notes.9: …Nfd7 retreats; the knight will support …c5 later.
notes.11: …Qxe7 recaptures; next Black aims for …c5 and …Nc6.

lines.summary: Develop with …Nf6 and …Be7, then retreat …Nfd7 and prepare …c5.

lines.name: Advance: 6.Be2

notes.11: …cxd4 opens the c-file before White can keep the chain with c3.
notes.13: …Nh6 heads for f5, adding a fourth attacker on d4.

lines.name: Winawer: 7.Qg4

notes.12: Qg4 attacks g7, which the dark-squared bishop no longer defends.
notes.13: …Qc7 counterattacks e5 and c3 instead of defending g7.
